correctness.rationale: In Laurent polynomials A=x^-1+1+x satisfies A³=A(x³)+3(x^-2+2x^-1+2+2x+x²). Expanding modulo 9 yields T_(3m)=T_m+6mT_(m-1), T_(3m+1)=T_m+3m(T_m+5T_(m-1)), T_(3m+2)=3(m+1)T_m (mod 9). Their mod-3 reduction is the known presence-of-a-2 digit test. Read ternary digits from most significant: a second 2 forces zero mod9, while one 2 preceded immediately by 1 becomes zero only once a following digit appears. The no-2 and exceptional singleton-2 classes yield exactly 3^k-(k+6)2^(k-2) for k>=2. Independently computed 2001 recurrence terms and matched the digit predicate throughout; not extrapolated to infinity.
